planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in deep, well-drained soil; Shelly is a vigorous but compact grower bred in Israel from a Tommy Atkins x Keitt cross and bears fruit precociously, often by its third year.

directions: Shelly is a late-season Israeli mango cultivar developed at the Volcani Center as a cross of Tommy Atkins and Keitt, bred to extend the export harvest window into fall. Fruit is large, round, and apple-shaped with no pronounced beak, turning orange with a red blush at maturity, and the firm, fibreless flesh holds its quality at room temperature for weeks after picking, an unusual trait among mangoes. Harvest runs from September into mid-November, well after most Florida and Caribbean cultivars have finished, making it useful for extending a home mango season in warm climates. Provide full sun, deep well-drained soil, and protection from any frost, since the tree is strictly tropical to warm-subtropical.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Mango Growing in the Florida Home Landscape

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil with room to spread; Maya is a regular, heavy-bearing cultivar and Israel's top commercial mango for European export.

directions: Maya arose as a chance seedling in an Israeli orchard and was named for the grower's wife; it has since become the single most widely planted commercial mango cultivar in Israel. The plump, ovate fruit is medium-sized, yellow with a reddish blush, and shows a small, distinctive 'horn' at the stylar end, with firm, juicy, aromatic, nearly fiber-free flesh of high eating quality. It ripens in early summer, ahead of most other Israeli cultivars, and is a dependable, regular annual bearer with a small monoembryonic stone. Grow in full sun on deep, well-drained soil and keep the tree frost-free, as mango wood is easily damaged by cold.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil; Omer was selected by an Israeli grower and named for one of their children, and ripens mid-season between the earlier Maya and later Shelly cultivars.

directions: Omer is a mid-season Israeli mango cultivar with round, apple-shaped fruit of medium size, its orange-yellow skin heavily blushed red-purple for a striking appearance in the orchard. The opulent yellow flesh is firm and virtually fiber-free with a strong, sweet, succulent flavor that has made it a favorite in both domestic and export markets. Harvest typically falls in late July into August in Israel's Mediterranean climate, slotting between earlier and later cultivars to help growers spread out their picking season. Site trees in full sun with deep, well-drained soil and keep them free of frost, as with other mango cultivars.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in deep, well-drained soil; Ettinger is a Type B flowering cultivar selected in Israel in 1947 and is traditionally planted alongside Type A cultivars such as Hass for cross-pollination.

directions: Ettinger was selected as a seedling of Fuerte near Kefar Malal, Israel, and released commercially in 1947, making it one of the oldest avocado cultivars developed outside California. It is a Mexican x Guatemalan hybrid bearing large, smooth, thin, bright-green fruit that stays green as it ripens, enclosing mild, buttery flesh with relatively low oil content. For decades it has served as Israel's primary commercial pollinator for Hass, since its Type B flowering habit complements Hass's Type A flowers and its early harvest window from September through January bridges the gap before other cultivars mature. Grow in full sun with excellent drainage, since avocado roots are highly sensitive to Phytophthora root rot in waterlogged ground.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in deep, well-drained soil; Iriet is a Type B flowering cultivar developed at Israel's Akko Experiment Station from a Hass outcross and is grown as a Hass pollinator with its own marketable fruit.

directions: Iriet was developed at the Akko Experiment Station in Israel's Western Galilee from a Hass outcross, producing a small-to-medium, slightly weeping tree well suited to higher-density plantings. The glossy fruit closely resembles Hass, turning from green to black as it ripens, and encloses rich, buttery, fiber-free yellow flesh with a green rim around an unusually small seed. As a Type B flowering cultivar harvested from January through April, it is an effective pollinator for Hass while also producing good-quality fruit of its own. Grow in full sun on deep, well-drained soil, as with other avocado cultivars, and avoid overwatering to limit root rot risk.
sources: ScienceDirect — Scientia Horticulturae (Iriet and Ettinger SNP pollinator study)

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in deep, well-drained soil; Arad is a precocious Israeli selection from the Volcani Center's breeding program that can begin bearing by its second year after grafting.

directions: Arad was selected from a seedling breeding program at the Volcani Center in Bet Dagan, Israel, and is notable for both precocious bearing and very high yields, reportedly outperforming Hass by roughly half in Israeli trials. Fruit ripens green-skinned like Fuerte, with a medium-thick, easily separated peel over fiber-free, buttery yellow flesh with a green rim around a small seed, and it can be harvested stem-free without damaging the skin. Harvest in Israel runs from January through April, similar to Fuerte, and the fruit stores well for about four weeks under refrigeration. Grow in full sun with deep, well-drained soil, allowing room for a vigorous, productive canopy.

planting.note: Start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm soil after danger of frost has passed; Geumssaragi-Euncheon is the most widely grown chamoe cultivar in South Korea since its 1984 introduction.

directions: Geumssaragi-Euncheon ('gold dust Euncheon') was bred by Hungnong Seeds in 1984 as an improved selection of the older Euncheon chamoe line, and quickly became the standard chamoe grown across South Korea. The oblong fruit shows the cultivar's namesake golden-yellow skin flecked and striped with fine white lines, enclosing crisp, very sweet white flesh with the delicate floral fragrance typical of oriental melons. Vines are vigorous and productive on trellis or mulched ground, and fruit should be picked at full color break since chamoe does not ripen further or store well after harvest. Keep soil consistently moist through fruit set and reduce watering slightly as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate sweetness.
sources: bburi kitchen — Korean Melon (Chamoe) variety notes

planting.note: Direct-sow or transplant after soil has warmed and all frost danger has passed; Danhobak is a compact, bushy kabocha-type squash well suited to home gardens.

directions: Danhobak, whose name simply means 'sweet pumpkin' in Korean, is a small kabocha-type winter squash of Cucurbita maxima prized for its dense, deep-orange, remarkably sweet flesh. The compact, somewhat flattened fruit has a dark green, lightly ribbed rind that cures to a dull finish in storage, and the thick flesh is the base for hobakjuk, Korea's traditional sweet pumpkin porridge, as well as soups and steamed side dishes. Plants form manageable bush-to-semi-vining growth that fits smaller gardens better than large sprawling squash. Harvest when the rind resists piercing with a fingernail and cure fruit in a warm, dry spot for a week or two before storing to further concentrate sweetness.
sources: Korean Bapsang — Hobakjuk and Danhobak notes

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out once soil has warmed; Subicho is a traditional landrace from the Subi area of Yeongyang county, a region famous for red pepper growing since before 1950.

directions: Subicho is a traditional Korean red pepper landrace cultivated in the Subi area of Yeongyang county, Gyeongbuk province, since before 1950, long regarded as a benchmark variety for Korean red pepper quality. The slender, thin-walled fruit ripens from green to deep red and is valued for a balanced profile that is both sweet and spicy rather than sharply hot, making it a preferred choice for both fresh use and drying into gochugaru powder. Because the open-pollinated landrace is susceptible to Phytophthora capsici and viral disease, modern backcross-improved lines carrying resistance genes are now grown alongside the traditional type. Grow in full sun with consistent moisture and good drainage, staking plants as they become heavy with fruit.
sources: Acta Horticulturae — 'Breeding a landrace of capsicum pepper in Yeongyang, Subicho'
PMC — NMR-Based Metabolomic Analysis of Korean Landrace Red Pepper cv. Subicho
